title: BUILD-001-oss-stack-decision-matrix
universal_lens: The OSS stack decision matrix formalizes a constrained optimization over a discrete configuration space of open-source components. It defines a bounded state-transition manifold where integration feasibility is governed by strict topological boundaries—specifically license compatibility and security isolation—ensuring the system remains within a provably safe operational subspace before any production deployment.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this matrix acts as a conformal prediction filter for external data pipelines. We treat unverified OSS integrations as high-variance noise; the decision matrix applies Bayesian priors on legal and security risks, dynamically updating posterior probabilities to ensure only statistically robust, low-risk architectural shifts are permitted into the core inference engine.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the matrix dictates a rigid state-transition protocol: moving from 'sandbox' to 'production' requires explicit eigenvalue thresholds of trust. It prevents catastrophic state collapse by enforcing a docs-first boundary condition, ensuring that all operational workflows maintain structural integrity and reversible rollback capabilities during dynamic market shifts.

primitives.name: OSS Leverage Workflow Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why It Matters This improves decision quality, revenue, speed, support, retention, trust, or cost savings by converting open-source leverage into a bounded GSE workflow.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Decision Quality (DQ): dimensionless metric [0,1]; Cost Savings (CS): USD; Bounded Workflow (BW): Topological constraint set.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes open-source components can be mathematically mapped to internal value metrics without violating existing IP constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the bounding function fails to contain external dependencies, leading to uncontrolled technical debt or license contamination.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a constrained Hamiltonian system where external energy (OSS) is injected but strictly confined by potential wells (GSE workflows).
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in manual coordination hours and measurable SaaS cost displacement.

primitives.name: Legal & Security Boundary Condition
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Security Boundary No secrets, production data, customer PII, proprietary method docs, payment data, or production source keys.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Secrets (S): Cryptographic entropy; PII: Identifiable data vectors; Production Data (PD): Live state tensors.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a perfectly isolated sandbox environment exists where boundary conditions can be strictly enforced via zero-trust architecture.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if the sandbox leaks, causing cross-contamination between the evaluation manifold and the production state space.

layer2.mapping: Derives a hard kernel cutoff function that zeroes out any interaction term involving sensitive production variables during the evaluation phase.
layer2.telemetry: Zero incidents of PII exposure or secret rotation triggered by sandbox evaluations.

primitives.name: Docs-First Sandbox Initialization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Start in docs or a sandbox and only move into app code after explicit approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Approval Threshold (A): Boolean gate; Sandbox State (SS): Isolated computational environment.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes documentation serves as a sufficient proxy for initial system dynamics before committing to executable code changes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if implicit approvals bypass the explicit gate, resulting in undocumented state mutations in the production branch.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to a two-stage Markov Decision Process where the transition probability to the 'app code' state is zero unless an explicit reward signal (approval) is received.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of documented design specs to merged PRs; latency between spec approval and code commit.

Mathematically, we define a state space \( \mathcal{S} \) representing the current GSE architecture. The introduction of an OSS component represents a perturbation vector \( \vec{v}_{oss} \). To prevent systemic instability, we impose a strict bounding operator \( \mathcal{B} \), derived from the 'legal_security_boundary' primitive, which projects \( \vec{v}_{oss} \) onto a safe subspace \( \mathcal{S}_{safe} \). This projection explicitly zeroes out any components interacting with production secrets or PII. The 'docs_first_sandbox' primitive introduces a temporal discretization to the state transition. The system cannot evolve from state \( t \) (documentation/sandbox) to \( t+1 \) (application code) unless a specific eigenvalue threshold of 'explicit approval' is met. This creates a gated dynamical system. The 'oss_leverage_workflow' acts as the objective function \( J \), optimizing for decision quality and cost savings while remaining constrained by \( \mathcal{B} \). Failure modes arise primarily from boundary leakage—if \( \mathcal{B} \) is porous, the perturbation \( \vec{v}_{oss} \) introduces uncontrollable variance (security breaches or license violations) into \( \mathcal{S} \). Thus, the matrix is not merely a checklist, but a rigorous mathematical safeguard ensuring that the integration of external leverage does not compromise the topological integrity of the proprietary sports intelligence engine.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the 'Founder/Internal Actor' as a utility maximizer seeking to reduce cognitive load and manual coordination overhead. Conversely, the 'External OSS Ecosystem' is modeled as a chaotic agent introducing hidden dependencies and license entanglements. The decision matrix acts as a game-theoretic equilibrium point, where the internal actor enforces strict rules to neutralize the chaotic intent of the external ecosystem, ensuring that adoption yields net positive utility without exposing the core intellectual property to adversarial extraction or accidental contamination.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: An anti-collinearity veto is triggered if the proposed OSS integration exhibits high correlation with existing proprietary methods, risking IP dilution or redundant complexity. A leakage veto activates if telemetry indicates any data flow crossing from the isolated sandbox into production databases prior to the explicit approval gate. Furthermore, if the legal compliance layer detects a non-zero probability of AGPL/MPL viral licensing contamination, a hard veto overrides the optimization objective, forcing an immediate rollback to preserve the closed-source nature of the GSE core.
